what_it_is: Paperthin (npm package paperthin 0.17.7, MIT) is a catalog of 28 agent skills: plain-Markdown SKILL.md prompt modules in four groups (depth, breadth, coil, mesh). They package old engineering habits such as single source of truth, independent review, falsification, leakage audits, clean rewrites and handoff from live state as reflexes an agent runs by name or by description match; twelve are user-invoked only and sixteen can also be triggered by the model. The only executable code is a small discovery-notice hook (a shared Node core with a Claude Code/Codex SessionStart command adapter and an OpenCode plugin adapter), plus CI drift guards and tag-triggered release automation that keep the hand-copied roster consistent. Nothing in it enforces agent behavior: every pattern is fail-open guidance, the efficacy evidence is narrative and points into a gitignored local folder, and only the frontmatter gate has tests.
architecture: Skill catalog: 28 plain-Markdown prompt modules with name/description frontmatter and Goal/Workflow/Rules/Verification sections (skills/<perspective>/<name>/SKILL.md)
Authoring contract: philosophy, layout, SKILL.md anatomy, rule-copy map, shipping and releasing checklists (AGENTS.md)
Invocation policy: model-invoked versus user-invoked split and per-skill rationale (docs/invocation.md)
User docs: English README with Index, Problem, Fixes and [PROOF] narratives, plus 10 index-only localized copies that point to the English Fixes section (README.md, docs/readme/README.*.md)
Claude Code entry points: bare-text pointer to AGENTS.md and plugin manifest listing all skill paths (CLAUDE.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json)
Shared notice core: roster array, installed-skill probe, notice text, state paths (scripts/catalog.cjs)
Command-hook adapter: fail-open SessionStart discovery notice for Claude Code and Codex (scripts/session-check.cjs)
Plugin adapter: OpenCode system.transform notice with re-injection guard (scripts/opencode-discovery.js)

CI drift guards: catalog structure, dual-YAML frontmatter parse (with tests), skill references, relative links, catalog set equality, deploy-home SSOT (scripts/validate-skills.sh, scripts/check-frontmatter.cjs, scripts/check-frontmatter.test.cjs, scripts/check-skill-refs.sh, scripts/check-links.sh, scripts/check-catalog-sync.cjs, scripts/check-deploy-home.cjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml)
Release pipeline: signed-tag trigger, validation, version equals tag, skip-if-published npm publish with provenance, create-or-edit GitHub Release (.github/workflows/release.yml)
Installer/upgrader skill: reconciliation against a rename table and the catalog, SessionStart hook wiring by remote fetch, optional repository star (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md)
Dev helpers: symlink skills into ~/.claude/skills, list skills (scripts/link-skills.sh, scripts/list-skills.sh)
Local provenance outside the repo: gitignored .re0/ iteration casebooks and release notes (AGENTS.md:73-77, .gitignore:3)
Package metadata: one devDependency, yaml 2.9.1 (package.json, package-lock.json); text-only SVG assets with no scripts (assets/*.svg)

atoms.name: SKILL.md on-demand prompt modules
atoms.statement: Each of the 28 patterns ships as a self-contained Markdown skill whose frontmatter description is the model-facing trigger and whose body has Goal, Workflow, Rules and a self-run Verification section.
atoms.mechanism: Skills live at skills/<perspective>/<name>/SKILL.md with name/description frontmatter (AGENTS.md:39-54); the host loads a model-invoked skill when its description matches, and cross-skill use is by prose invocation, never ../ links (docs/invocation.md:6,33; scripts/validate-skills.sh:56). CI enforces the four sections, name equal to directory and an 800-character description cap (scripts/validate-skills.sh:45-67).
principle_conflict: P8: a skill is advice the model may never load; it proves no fact
Z1: activation and the Verification section both depend on the model's own choice and self-check
P6: G1 controls the agent only through hooks
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as a G1 mechanism: skills stay the host's native capability (P2). Anything G1 must guarantee goes through hooks, and any habit G1 wants delivered goes through measured PreInvocation injection.

atoms.name: Reach-bias: hide action-biasing reflexes
atoms.statement: Skills whose mere presence would bias the agent toward an action (commit, publish, demolition, chronic self-doubt) are user-invoked only, so the model cannot reach them and no skill can chain one user-invoked skill into another.
atoms.mechanism: Frontmatter disable-model-invocation: true removes the model-facing trigger, and twelve skills carry it with a per-skill bias rationale (docs/invocation.md:5,8,14-27); orchestrators are told never to fire them (skills/depth/sip/SKILL.md:28; skills/coil/nba/SKILL.md:28). Frontmatter, the README Invoker column and docs/invocation.md agree on the same twelve, but no CI check guards that agreement.
principle_conflict: P8: hiding a prompt proves nothing; it transfers only as a rule about what G1 injects
atoms.proof_purpose: none for authority; measurement fact that injected text without action-inviting reflexes does not raise the false-completion rate
atoms.g1_design: INJECT-content rule: G1's injected text never contains action-inviting reflexes such as 'commit when done' or 'reply DONE'; variants are A/B-tested on the false-completion rate in the measurement layer, never treated as a guarantee.

atoms.name: Unpinned global install with auto-updating symlinks
atoms.statement: Installation is one npx skills@latest command for every agent, run from an elevated shell when needed so skills are symlinked and auto-update, and users are invited to paste it into an agent and say 'set this up for me'.
atoms.mechanism: README.md:21-29 gives the command and the agent-delegated setup; re0-upgrade wraps npx skills list/add/update/remove and requires one -s <name> per catalog entry instead of --all (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:57-60,83-84). The dev linker symlinks a checkout into ~/.claude/skills, refusing a self-referencing destination but rm -rf'ing any real directory with a matching name (scripts/link-skills.sh:10-22,32-36).
principle_conflict: Z6: upstream text auto-updates into every agent's standing instructions with no review or pin
Z1: installation is delegated to the agent
P3: agent instructions become a moving external dependency
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT: G1 installs only vendored, hash-pinned hook files through its own one-time bootstrap and never lets upstream text flow into agent context. The 'enumerate each name, never --all' habit is kept in the bootstrap (PTH-19).

atoms.name: Claude Code plugin manifest and shadow installs
atoms.statement: A .claude-plugin/plugin.json registers all 28 skill paths so a clone can load as a Claude Code plugin, which the skills CLI cannot see and re0-upgrade must detect as a 'shadow install'.
atoms.mechanism: plugin.json lists ./skills/... paths (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:4-33); validate-skills.sh requires every skill to be registered and every registered path to resolve (scripts/validate-skills.sh:54,73-76); re0-upgrade flags a loaded plugin that the CLI lists as empty and refuses to delete it or install a second copy (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:41-43).
principle_conflict: P7: host-specific packaging
P8: proves no fact
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT: G1 has no plugin surface; its only delivery is the two agy hooks.json layers.

atoms.name: Bare-text CLAUDE.md pointer to AGENTS.md
atoms.statement: AGENTS.md is the one canonical instruction file for agents and contributors (README is human-only), and Claude Code is pointed at it by a CLAUDE.md whose entire content is the text 'AGENTS.md'.
atoms.mechanism: CLAUDE.md:1 is a regular file (git mode 100644) holding the bare string AGENTS.md, not an @-import or a symlink, while AGENTS.md:81 claims Claude Code 'reaches it through the one-line CLAUDE.md'; delivery therefore depends on the model choosing to open the file. AGENTS.md:81 and skills/coil/re0-plan/SKILL.md:30 also split registers: agent mechanism in AGENTS.md, user-facing content in README.
principle_conflict: Z1: standing instructions that the model may skip are fail-open
P3: instruction files are agent-writable and are not state
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT: G1 delivers its contract text through SessionStart/PreInvocation injection computed from its own state; any instruction-file copy is an optional mirror that G1 never relies on.

atoms.name: Fail-open SessionStart notice hook
atoms.statement: A SessionStart command hook injects a discovery notice into the model's context, exits 0 with valid JSON on every path, stays silent when it cannot tell, and throttles itself to once per 24 hours with a stamp file.
atoms.mechanism: session-check.cjs prints either a hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext notice or {continue:true, suppressOutput:true} and wraps all logic in try/catch (scripts/session-check.cjs:21-32,48-57); a ~/.re0/last-notice.json stamp enforces the window (scripts/session-check.cjs:19,34-46; scripts/catalog.cjs:38-39), and missingSkills returns null for 'cannot tell' (scripts/catalog.cjs:49-55). The stamp is shared by all hosts, and a stamp dated in the future keeps notices suppressed until 24 hours after that date.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection
principle_conflict: P8: wall-clock throttling proves nothing; G1 injection should be a function of ledger state
P3: the throttle stamp is mutable side state shared across hosts
atoms.proof_purpose: none (projection only; never part of the authority path)
atoms.g1_design: INJECT: G1's SessionStart projection is wrapped so every path prints a valid injectSteps object or nothing, and it recomputes its text from the ledger each session instead of throttling by clock; agy already treats SessionStart as fail-open.

atoms.name: Relay-cue phrasing with explicit do-not-act clause
atoms.statement: The injected notice is phrased as a cue for the model to relay to the human, plus an explicit prohibition on acting ('do NOT run /re0-upgrade or install anything yourself'), chosen because a relay test reportedly surfaced it on about two thirds of first turns.
atoms.mechanism: noticeText builds the cue and the prohibition (scripts/catalog.cjs:66-71); a comment cites a relay test in which this form beat an informational phrasing (scripts/catalog.cjs:63-65), with the casebook kept in gitignored .re0/ (scripts/catalog.cjs:12; .gitignore:3). session-check.cjs notes that hook output reaches the model, which must relay it to the human (scripts/session-check.cjs:10-11).
principle_conflict: Z5: the two-thirds figure is author-presented and unverifiable
P4: a relay or compliance rate is a measurement, never a guarantee
atoms.proof_purpose: none for authority; measurement fact 'injected variant A yields rate p (with CI) against variant B'
atoms.g1_design: MEASURE: treat the wording of injected text as an A/B variable in G1's measurement layer (ensembles with confidence intervals), for example a declarative ledger fact plus an explicit 'do not claim completion; G1 decides' clause versus the bare fact, scored on the false-completion rate.

atoms.name: Compaction-safe idempotent prompt injection
atoms.statement: The OpenCode adapter injects the notice at most once per session and skips injection when a rebuilt, post-compaction system prompt already contains the notice marker.
atoms.mechanism: A per-plugin Set of session IDs and a substring check for 'paperthin discovery notice' guard output.system.push inside the system.transform hook, and all errors are swallowed (scripts/opencode-discovery.js:39-61).
principle_conflict: P8: justified only if agy injectSteps accumulate across PreInvocation calls or compaction, which is unmeasured
atoms.proof_purpose: none (projection hygiene: at most one copy of G1's projection in model context)
atoms.g1_design: RESEARCH: measure whether agy ephemeralMessage steps persist or accumulate across PreInvocation calls and context compaction; only if they do, tag the projection with the ledger head hash and skip re-injection when that head is already present.

atoms.name: Shared core with thin host adapters
atoms.statement: Roster and notice logic live in one shared module that a command-hook adapter (Claude Code, Codex) and a JS plugin adapter (OpenCode) both import, so host differences stay inside the adapters.
atoms.mechanism: catalog.cjs declares itself the single code home for both adapters and exports the shared functions and paths (scripts/catalog.cjs:2-12,73-76); session-check.cjs is the class-A command-hook adapter and opencode-discovery.js the class-B plugin adapter, loading the core through createRequire (scripts/session-check.cjs:3-17; scripts/opencode-discovery.js:1-21).
atoms.proof_purpose: none (structural: keeps agy output shapes and decision semantics out of core semantics, P7)
atoms.g1_design: STRUCTURE: G1 core (ledger, contract, gate decisions as pure functions) returns host-neutral verdicts; one agy adapter maps them to agy JSON (empty stdout for no decision, never {} or allow, deny/ask/force_ask, injectSteps, Stop continue) and holds the measured agy facts.

atoms.name: State path defined once; retired names tombstoned
atoms.statement: The runtime state directory is defined in exactly one module and imported everywhere, and a CI guard fails if the retired home name reappears in shipped runtime or installer prose, with no legacy fallback or migrator by design.
atoms.mechanism: STATE_DIR and NOTICE_STAMP are defined and exported once (scripts/catalog.cjs:34-39,75), with the no-migration decision stated at scripts/catalog.cjs:35-37; check-deploy-home.cjs asserts the exports exist, scans the three runtime files line by line for the retired '.paperthin' segment, and checks re0-upgrade's prose (scripts/check-deploy-home.cjs:6-16,22-67).
principle_conflict: P3: silently abandoning old state is wrong for a ledger; G1 must refuse unknown versions loudly
atoms.proof_purpose: every G1 component reads and writes the same canonical state root, and no retired or P8-rejected mechanism identifier is present in shipped G1 core
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in G1's test suite: one constants module owns the state root and ledger paths; a tombstone list of deleted mechanisms is grepped across shipped core and must return zero hits; the ledger carries a schema version and G1 fails closed on an unknown version instead of migrating silently.

atoms.name: Guarded copies: exact equality enforced
atoms.statement: When a fact must physically exist in several places (units ship alone and there is no build step), the copies are kept and a deterministic CI guard fails on any divergence; where a pointer suffices, copies are replaced by a pointer to one canonical home.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:9 names the roster copies and forbids deduplicating them; check-catalog-sync.cjs extracts backticked names under '## Current catalog' and requires exact set equality with CATALOG (scripts/check-catalog-sync.cjs:17-41), and validate-skills.sh requires the package.json and plugin.json descriptions to match (scripts/validate-skills.sh:37-42). The guard checks set, not order (AGENTS.md:86), its own header still says '21-skill' for a 28-name roster (scripts/check-catalog-sync.cjs:6; scripts/catalog.cjs:19-24), and translations point to the English Fixes section instead of copying it (docs/readme/README.ko.md:130).
atoms.proof_purpose: two copies of one fact are exactly equal; in G1, the G1 entries registered in the global and workspace hooks.json files (and the hook script hashes) equal the set recorded at bootstrap
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: wherever G1 must duplicate a fact it checks exact equality, never similarity. The global (root-of-trust) PreToolUse hook compares the G1 entries in .agents/hooks.json and the G1 script hashes with the bootstrap record and denies mutating tools on mismatch, which catches an agent that rewrote hooks.json for the next session; facts are kept out of comments, which no guard covers.
encodes: single source of truth by enforced equality

atoms.name: Strict dual-parser frontmatter gate
atoms.statement: Every skill's YAML frontmatter must parse strictly, with unique keys, under both YAML 1.1 and 1.2, because the two hosts that load skills use those parsers and silently drop a skill that one of them misreads.
atoms.mechanism: check-frontmatter.cjs parses the frontmatter with eemeli/yaml in strict, uniqueKeys mode once per version, reports file:line:column, and requires a mapping with a string description (scripts/check-frontmatter.cjs:1,7-24); two node:test cases pin the original failure and duplicate-key rejection (scripts/check-frontmatter.test.cjs:8-15), and CI runs both (.github/workflows/ci.yml:17-18; scripts/validate-skills.sh:70-71).
atoms.proof_purpose: each canonical G1 record (ledger entry, contract, receipt, hooks.json) has exactly one interpretation, so the hash that binds it binds one meaning
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in the ledger library: parse canonical JSON strictly and reject duplicate keys (stock JSON.parse and Python json.loads silently keep the last one), invalid UTF-8 and trailing data before hashing; serialize canonically; validate hooks.json the way agy reads it (camelCase keys); keep a regression test that a duplicate-key record is rejected.
encodes: be strict in what you accept

atoms.name: Catalog lint: structure, links, orphans, typos
atoms.statement: CI checks that every skill has the required sections, a name equal to its directory, registration in plugin.json and README, no deep ../ references, resolvable relative links, reachability from README, and no near-miss skill-name typos.
atoms.mechanism: validate-skills.sh accumulates errors and fails once at the end (scripts/validate-skills.sh:8-9,44-82); check-links.sh resolves inline and reference links on disk (scripts/check-links.sh:37-109); check-skill-refs.sh runs a one-affix typo heuristic and an orphan guard (scripts/check-skill-refs.sh:41-69); ci.yml runs them on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6,19-24).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate that binds artifacts and output digests
principle_conflict: P8: the structure checks are weaker than G1's contract coverage matrix, reference resolution is already covered by T1's artifact and digest binding, and the typo heuristic is approximate rather than exact
atoms.proof_purpose: none beyond facts G1 already proves
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as separate mechanisms; keep only the habit of collecting every violation before failing in G1's own test runner.

atoms.name: Gates need negative controls
atoms.statement: The guards document that a piped while-read loop runs in a subshell and silently swallows failures (a green gate that cannot fail), yet only one of the six guards ships a test proving it can fail.
atoms.mechanism: check-skill-refs.sh and check-links.sh feed their loops through process substitution precisely so fail=1 propagates (scripts/check-skill-refs.sh:42-45; scripts/check-links.sh:72-73); the only negative test is the frontmatter case (scripts/check-frontmatter.test.cjs:8-14); re0-merge asks for a throwaway regression case to prove a contributor's fix (skills/depth/re0-merge/SKILL.md:17).
atoms.proof_purpose: each G1 gate is non-vacuous: a known-bad fixture makes it deny, so a pass from that gate carries information
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in G1 self-test: every gate (PreToolUse write locks, completion hash and subset checks, ledger chain verification, Stop continuation) ships a negative-control fixture that must produce deny or fail; a gate whose negative control passes is marked untrusted, and the self-test receipt records each gate's hash with its negative-control outcome.

atoms.name: Tag-triggered release with exact version gate
atoms.statement: A pushed signed tag triggers CI that validates the catalog, requires package.json's version to equal the tag exactly, publishes with npm provenance only if the version is not already published, and creates or edits the GitHub Release idempotently; CI never signs or creates commits or tags.
atoms.mechanism: release.yml: tag trigger and OIDC permissions (.github/workflows/release.yml:3-9), version-equals-tag check (27-31), skip-if-published npm publish (33-42), create-or-edit release from the annotated tag message (44-57). AGENTS.md:97,108-113 make the signed tag the human trust boundary and publishing CI-only from a clean checkout; re0-release checks the version locally before pushing (skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:38).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding receipt sequence/hash and the current source and tree
atoms.proof_purpose: a completion is recorded at most once per (task, receipt hash), and only when the receipt-bound identity equals the current identity exactly
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: G1's completion append is idempotent, so re-running completion for the same task and receipt hash is a no-op rather than a second entry, and the exact check (receipt-bound tree hash equals current tree hash) runs immediately before the append, as version-equals-tag runs before publish.
encodes: exact identity check before an irreversible step

atoms.name: Never hand-run a harness-owned step
atoms.statement: Steps the release workflow owns are never run by hand, not even to rescue a failed run, because a hand-run step drops what the workflow adds (provenance attestation, title convention) while still looking like a good release.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:109 and skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:29,36,49 state the rule and require fixing the cause and re-running the workflow; the one exception is re-pushing a re-cut tag so the workflow still does the rest (skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:36).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself in a scrubbed environment
atoms.proof_purpose: every receipt and ledger entry was written by G1's own process, not by the agent
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: PreToolUse denies agent file writes and shell commands that target G1's state directory, receipts, hooks.json files or verifier entry points (exact path match on tool arguments, best-effort for shell strings), and the ledger accepts only hash-chained entries appended by G1, so an agent-authored 'receipt' fails even if a write slips through.

atoms.name: Re-cut a broken tag at the same version
atoms.statement: A tag whose message, signature or target the author got wrong is deleted and re-cut at the same version instead of rolling forward, so one version name can denote different tag objects over time.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:109 and skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:29,36 permit deleting and re-pushing such a tag, and the HEAD commit is exactly this policy change ('fix: re-cut a tag the author broke instead of rolling the version forward'). Meanwhile re0-upgrade pins downloaded hook scripts to the v<installed-version> tag (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:65).
principle_conflict: P5: a receipt must bind an immutable identity, and a re-cuttable name is not one
Z7: a mutable tag pin is not a verified pin
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT: G1 identifies receipts, contracts and hook scripts by content hash only; names (tags, versions, task labels) never serve as the binding identity, and a correction is a new ledger entry, never a re-cut under the same identifier.

atoms.name: Signed commits and tags as trust boundary
atoms.statement: Signed tags and signed, cleaned commits are the human's trust boundary, checked with git tag -v and %G? = G before pushing.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:97,108 make signed tags the trust boundary and require a good-signature check before push; re0-git re-commits with -S and verifies %G? (skills/depth/re0-git/SKILL.md:21,29,35); re0-release verifies the tag signature (skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:28).
principle_conflict: P6: signing needs a human key ceremony
Z5: a key readable by the agent's OS user adds no trust against the agent
atoms.proof_purpose: a ledger head anchor was produced with G1's key and not by the agent, but only if the key is outside the agent's reach
atoms.g1_design: RESEARCH: signing the ledger head adds trust only if the key lives outside the agent's OS user (separate user, hardware token, or a keyring that requires presence); otherwise G1 relies on hash chaining plus a head anchor stored where agent tools are denied.

atoms.name: Idempotent non-clobbering hook installer
atoms.statement: re0-upgrade converges an install by classifying names as stale, missing, present or unknown against a rename table and the catalog, printing a plan, running only the planned commands, retrying a failed item once, and wiring a SessionStart hook only if none already runs the script by any path, after a config backup and without touching foreign hooks.
atoms.mechanism: Rename SSOT and catalog (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:13-33); classification, plan, confirmation, exactly the planned commands, and one retry before a confirmed reinstall (45-61); backup, dedupe by any path, no deletion or overwrite of another tool's hook, and a report on how to unwire (64-69); unknown names stay untouched and wiring must exist exactly once (79, 94).
principle_conflict: Z1: in paperthin the agent performs the wiring from prose; G1 must do it in deterministic bootstrap code
P6: per-step human confirmation is replaced by G1's own post-state verification
atoms.proof_purpose: after bootstrap each hooks.json layer holds exactly one G1 entry per event with the expected command and script hash, and every foreign entry is byte-identical to before
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in G1's one-time bootstrap: parse both hooks.json layers, classify entries as g1-current, g1-stale or foreign, rewrite only G1 entries (identified by script hash, not path), back up with the backup hash recorded in the ledger, verify the post-state by exact set equality, and make re-running a no-op; the recorded set feeds the live check in PTH-11.
encodes: do no harm to foreign state

atoms.name: Remote tag-pinned fetch of hook code
atoms.statement: The upgrade skill downloads executable hook scripts from raw.githubusercontent.com at the installed version's tag into ~/.re0/ and registers them as SessionStart commands in Claude Code and Codex configs.
atoms.mechanism: skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:65-67 fetch catalog.cjs, session-check.cjs and (for OpenCode) opencode-discovery.js by tag and add the SessionStart or plugin entry; no checksum step exists, and tags may be re-cut at the same version (AGENTS.md:109).
principle_conflict: Z6: remote code enters an auto-run hook with no content-hash check
P5: a tag name is not an immutable identity
P3: the hook runtime becomes an external, mutable dependency
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT: G1 hook scripts are vendored in the G1 repository and pinned by sha256 recorded at bootstrap; G1 never fetches executable hook code at install or run time.

atoms.name: Static host matrix versus measured host contract
atoms.statement: Hook wiring supports only Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode and skips Copilot CLI, Grok Build and Antigravity CLI, asserting that Antigravity has no session-start event, while README claims the suite runs on any agent including Antigravity.
atoms.mechanism: skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:68 holds the skip list and README.md:9 lists Antigravity as supported; re0-release adds 'never invent or assume a CLI command or flag; verify it against official docs or a real run' (skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:35). G1's measured agy 1.1.27 facts show SessionStart works (undocumented), so the matrix entry is stale.
principle_conflict: Z7: a documented-only capability claim proved wrong for agy 1.1.27
atoms.proof_purpose: the running agy version equals a version whose hook contract G1 has measured, so G1's fail-open and fail-closed assumptions hold for this session
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: the agy adapter stores the measured hook contract keyed by agy version (events, fail-open/closed behavior, empty-stdout and {} semantics, the 10-continue cap); SessionStart records the observed agy version in the ledger, and the completion gate refuses receipts from a session whose host version has not passed the contract re-test suite.

atoms.name: Consent-gated promotional repository star
atoms.statement: After a successful upgrade the skill asks once, through the host's structured question tool, whether to star the repository with the user's authenticated gh account, and only an explicitly submitted 'Star repository' choice authorizes the API call.
atoms.mechanism: skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:70-74 define the question, the refusal to infer consent from silence, preselection, upgrade approval or --yes, the gh auth status check, and the gh api -X PUT user/starred/LilMGenius/paperthin call; verification item 5 repeats it (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:95).
principle_conflict: P8: no proof purpose
Z6: a side effect on the user's account inside an install flow
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT. Its consent rule (authorization is never inferred from silence, preselection or an adjacent approval) is already implied by G1 deciding each call separately and never printing allow.

atoms.name: Gitignored local provenance casebooks
atoms.statement: Iteration casebooks and release notes live in a gitignored .re0/ directory described as history and scratch, never shipped and never canonical, yet the repository's design rationales and proofs point into it.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:73-77 and .gitignore:1-3 define and ignore it; code comments cite decisions stored there (scripts/catalog.cjs:12,37); re0-plan creates the folders and re0-release retires them (skills/coil/re0-plan/SKILL.md:16-21; skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:31).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant .harness records (history, plans, walkthroughs, handoffs, audits, metrics)
principle_conflict: Z5: evidence that exists only in an unshipped, unversioned folder cannot be checked by anyone else
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as state: G1's only canonical record is its ledger, and agent-written notes are never read as facts.

atoms.name: Trust the artifact, not the author
atoms.statement: A skill must either re-derive the work from what is true now or import outside eyes to test it, because the maker's in-session mind is the worst judge of whether the work is clear and correct.
atoms.mechanism: Stated as the first philosophy line and the brand tagline (AGENTS.md:7; README.md:5; assets/thumbnail.svg:60) and applied only as prose, for example the separate-reader rule in shower and the in-session-bias rationale in sip (skills/depth/shower/SKILL.md:25; skills/depth/sip/SKILL.md:10,24).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct (confirm against a primary source; trusted versus data channel)
principle_conflict: Z5: paperthin still trusts the artifact as read by a model; G1 trusts only evidence it produced itself
atoms.proof_purpose: none (doctrine)
atoms.g1_design: Already G1 doctrine in a stricter form: the artifact is judged by G1's deterministic verification and hashes, never by another model reading it.

atoms.name: Restraint: an empty pass changes nothing
atoms.statement: A pass that finds nothing to genuinely improve changes nothing, an empty findings list is a valid result, and drift or disagreement must never be invented to justify work.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:10 and README.md:121 state it, and the rule is copied into re0, ssotize, detool, debloat, factchk and prism (skills/depth/re0/SKILL.md:27; skills/breadth/ssotize/SKILL.md:33,35; skills/depth/detool/SKILL.md:32; skills/depth/debloat/SKILL.md:28; skills/depth/factchk/SKILL.md:24; skills/mesh/prism/SKILL.md:29). The only evidence is one self-referential anecdote (README.md:139-141).
atoms.proof_purpose: a Stop continuation is issued only when the deterministic failing set is non-empty
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in Stop control: emit continue only when the pass/fail vector contains at least one failing acceptance check; an all-pass vector ends the loop without inventing work, and an unrunnable check is UNKNOWN, never pass. This is implied by G1's Hamming-distance control and costs one explicit test.

atoms.name: Edit-safety: assert target, report MISS
atoms.statement: Every mutating skill must assert that each edit target exists and report a MISS rather than a silent no-op, edit unicode-safe, replace per occurrence rather than by blanket sweep, and script large structural moves.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:69 maps the rule copy into re0, ssotize, detool, reorder, debloat and dedash (skills/depth/re0/SKILL.md:33; skills/breadth/ssotize/SKILL.md:39; skills/depth/detool/SKILL.md:33; skills/depth/reorder/SKILL.md:27; skills/depth/debloat/SKILL.md:29; skills/depth/dedash/SKILL.md:33); nothing enforces it.
principle_conflict: Z1: as an agent habit it cannot be enforced; only G1's own writes can be held to it
atoms.proof_purpose: every G1 state mutation was applied against the expected prior state, with no lost update and no silent no-op
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in G1's own writes: every ledger append names the expected head hash and fails loudly on mismatch (a compare-and-swap precondition complementing T1's head anchor), and a G1 operation that matches nothing returns an explicit MISS that every gate treats as not done.

atoms.name: Negatives-as-corpus: archive, never delete
atoms.statement: 'Cut' means move to an archive, never delete: failed paths, descoped items, retired cycles and declined contributions are kept as data so later cycles can prove an anti-pattern is gone.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:70 maps the rule copy into re0-memo, re0-work, re0-loop, autobahn, re0-plan, re0-release and re0-merge (skills/coil/re0-memo/SKILL.md:30; skills/coil/re0-work/SKILL.md:27; skills/coil/re0-loop/SKILL.md:33; skills/depth/autobahn/SKILL.md:31; skills/coil/re0-plan/SKILL.md:31; skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:39; skills/depth/re0-merge/SKILL.md:25).
atoms.proof_purpose: failed receipts, rejected completions and superseded contracts remain in the hash chain, so no later claim can erase an earlier failure
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in the ledger: failing receipts, rejected completions and superseded contracts are appended and never rewritten, and re-verification appends a new receipt instead of replacing history.

atoms.name: git log as the cross-environment handoff
atoms.statement: re0-git rewrites a finished commit's message to a durable-facts-only standard (commit-economy) so a fresh session can continue from git log alone, keeping the tree byte-identical and re-signing the commit.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/re0-git/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 17-22 (sample the local style, rewrite, amend or commit-tree plus replay), 26-30 (message only, commit-economy, signing, no unconfirmed rewrite of pushed history), 34-36 (git diff empty, %G? = G, re-read the log alone); commit-economy is carried inline in re0-release (skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:25; AGENTS.md:71,93; README.md:317-330).
principle_conflict: Z4: a commit message is agent-authored narrative, not evidence
P3: git history is rewritable (re0-git itself amends and replays commits), so it is not G1 state
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as a handoff channel; G1 continuity comes from its ledger. The 'tree stays byte-identical' check survives inside the declared-scope invariant (PTH-29).

atoms.name: Declared-scope invariant checked by exact diff
atoms.statement: Several mutating patterns declare what may change and check it mechanically afterwards: a message-only rewrite must leave the tree byte-identical, a reorder must keep every item and change only positions, a compression must keep every load-bearing claim, and an upgrade may run only the commands its plan named.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/re0-git/SKILL.md:27,34 (git diff <old> <new> must be empty); skills/depth/reorder/SKILL.md:23,32 (nothing reworded, added or removed); skills/depth/debloat/SKILL.md:24,35; skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:57,93 (run only the planned commands; the confirmation gate held).
atoms.proof_purpose: every change made during the task lies inside the contract's declared write scope (the changed-path set is a subset of the allowed set)
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: the immutable contract declares an allowed path set and G1 snapshots a tree manifest at contract time; PreToolUse denies file-tool writes outside the set (best-effort for shell strings) and PostToolUse journals each mutating call; at Stop the completion gate diffs the tree against the snapshot and requires exact subset membership, otherwise deny.

atoms.name: Unknown is not empty: tri-state results
atoms.statement: When a probe cannot tell (no skills visible, an unparseable list, an unreachable source, a missing skill), the result is reported as unknown or skipped, never as empty, missing or clean, and an orchestrator states what it skipped and why.
atoms.mechanism: missingSkills returns null for 'cannot tell' and callers stay silent (scripts/catalog.cjs:49-55; scripts/session-check.cjs:50); 'a flaky read is not an empty install', and an unparseable list means stop and report (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:42,81); factchk flags rather than asserts without a source (skills/depth/factchk/SKILL.md:15); orchestrators degrade gracefully and name skipped checks (AGENTS.md:64; skills/depth/sip/SKILL.md:26).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection
atoms.proof_purpose: no gate decision treats an unrunnable, timed-out or unparseable check as pass
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: every G1 check returns PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN; in the authority path UNKNOWN denies completion exactly like FAIL, the projection shows it as unknown, and every skipped check is named in the receipt.
encodes: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence

atoms.name: Two independent enumerations must agree
atoms.statement: Before acting on an enumeration, re-enumerate by a different method and confirm it surfaces nothing the first missed, and cross-check a tool's report against the on-disk footprint before concluding something is absent.
atoms.mechanism: ssotize re-enumerates with a different search term, synonym or tool (skills/breadth/ssotize/SKILL.md:20); re0-upgrade treats a CLI listing of zero skills as suspect when catalog directories exist on disk and re-checks before concluding (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:41-43).
atoms.proof_purpose: the changed-file set used by the scope and tree checks is complete, because two independent enumerators agree exactly
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: at completion G1 derives the changed set twice, from git status including untracked and ignored files and from a content-hash walk against the contract-time manifest; any disagreement yields UNKNOWN and denies completion.

atoms.name: Author never self-assesses
atoms.statement: Judgment on clarity, a decision or a validation must come from a separate context-free sub-session that receives only the artifact or an abstract item, never the author's intent, reasoning or negotiation.
atoms.mechanism: shower, feynman, autobahn, macrothink and mandela all route judgment to a fresh context (skills/depth/shower/SKILL.md:15,25-26; skills/depth/feynman/SKILL.md:17,27; skills/depth/autobahn/SKILL.md:14,17,23; skills/depth/macrothink/SKILL.md:21; skills/depth/mandela/SKILL.md:34).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself in a scrubbed environment
principle_conflict: P4: a fresh model reviewer is still non-deterministic; in G1 the independent party is G1's deterministic verifier
atoms.proof_purpose: the party that judged completion is not the party that did the work
atoms.g1_design: Already G1 doctrine: G1 itself verifies at Stop; model-based fresh-context review is allowed only in the measurement layer (PTH-43).

atoms.name: A deny is never re-litigated in-session
atoms.statement: When a user disputes a bright-line exclusion, the pressured session does not re-decide it: the abstract item goes to a fresh context, the appeal and outcome are logged, repeated appeals are surfaced as a signal, and excluded asks are never posed just to see whether they pass.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/autobahn/SKILL.md:14 (appeal to a fresh context with the persuasion stripped), 24 (a same-session appeal is not a re-review; repeated appeals are a signal), 26 (never probe).
atoms.proof_purpose: a gate decision is a pure function of G1 state and tool arguments, so agent prose cannot change it, and exact repeats of denied calls are counted
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: PreToolUse decisions read only the ledger and the tool arguments, never the agent's explanation; G1 stores a hash of each denied call and counts exact repeats as revisits that feed the oscillation detector and Stop control.

atoms.name: macrothink: convergence is reassurance, never proof
atoms.statement: macrothink strips the session's framing, fans out 2-5 same-model fresh reads, reports divergence first, and forbids majority vote, averaging, and calling same-model convergence verified or proved; prism applies the same never-average rule.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/macrothink/SKILL.md:13 (divergence is the signal), 19-29 (strip bait, fan out, classify, cluster, report), 33-40 (no majority vote or averaging; convergence is not proof), 51; skills/mesh/prism/SKILL.md:11,27,30; the user-invoked rationale says convergence must not masquerade as automatic proof (docs/invocation.md:17,27).
principle_conflict: PH and P8: the fan-out itself makes the AI smarter and proves nothing; only the rule transfers
atoms.proof_purpose: no completion was ever granted on the basis of model agreement
atoms.g1_design: Keep only the rule as an authority-path invariant: no count of agreeing model outputs, a judge model included, can satisfy a G1 gate; model ensembles appear only in the measurement layer with confidence intervals. Reject the fan-out.

atoms.name: re0-memo: failures become hard gates
atoms.statement: re0-memo turns a finished or failed cycle into class-level lessons, anti-patterns and next-cycle gates, prefers hard gates over advice, and checks that a from-scratch agent could avoid the failure from the docs alone.
atoms.mechanism: skills/coil/re0-memo/SKILL.md:16-23 (workflow, clustering specifics into a root at 18 and the fresh-agent check at 23), 29 (escalate each specific complaint to its class), 31 (prefer hard gates over advice), 40-43 (every anti-pattern names the gate that catches it).
principle_conflict: Z4 and P3: the memo is agent-authored text and is never G1 state
atoms.proof_purpose: every observed G1 failure class has a deterministic regression fixture that fails on the original failure
atoms.g1_design: GOVERNANCE: each observed G1 failure (for example the measured 3-of-8 'DONE' replies after a blocked call) becomes a named failure class with a deterministic regression fixture in G1's suite, never just a new injected sentence.

atoms.name: re0-merge: default-deny admission of additions
atoms.statement: re0-merge declines additive contributions by default, admits new tooling only if it mechanizes a rule already enforced by hand, verifies fixes with a throwaway regression case, keeps contributor authorship, and approves before landing.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/re0-merge/SKILL.md:15 (default-deny; tooling must mechanize an existing hand-enforced rule; a new skill only for a real gap), 17 (verify, do not re-fix), 18 and 26 (authorship kept; maintainer edits as separate commits), 25 (decline with a thesis-tied reason); the landing flow is at AGENTS.md:99.
atoms.proof_purpose: none at runtime; governance: each admitted G1 mechanism names the existing proof obligation it mechanizes
atoms.g1_design: GOVERNANCE for P8: a proposed G1 mechanism is declined unless it mechanizes a proof obligation G1 already has and ships with its negative control (PTH-14); the burden is on the addition to show G1 is weaker without it.

atoms.name: re0-release: irreversible publication staked separately
atoms.statement: re0-release treats the local commit and the public tag-and-push as two separately confirmed moments, stops on any checklist gap instead of guessing past it, and watches the triggered workflow to completion ('confirmed, not assumed').
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:11 (two moments), 15-21 (checklist; stop on a gap), 26 and 28 (separate confirmations; signature check), 29 and 48 (watch the run; never assume it landed), 38 (local version check before push).
principle_conflict: P6: confirmations involve the user; acceptable only through agy's native permission prompt, never as a G1 interface
atoms.proof_purpose: no public, irreversible command (push, tag push, publish, release) ran without a native user confirmation
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: PreToolUse classifies irreversible public commands (git push, tag pushes, npm publish, gh release) and returns force_ask; how force_ask behaves in agy print mode is unmeasured and must be tested first, and completion still rests on G1 observing the outcome itself.
encodes: observe the outcome, don't assume it

atoms.name: re0-plan: never-empty casebook, evidence traces to design
atoms.statement: re0-plan creates an iteration folder and its first real file in the same step, so it is never empty, and requires every EVIDENCE gate to trace back to a DESIGN line, so no proof surface exists that the design never asked for.
atoms.mechanism: skills/coil/re0-plan/SKILL.md:16-20 (create the folder and write the first file in one motion), 26 and 38 (never empty), 32 and 39 (every EVIDENCE gate traces to DESIGN), 29 (the version bump stays provisional, judged by kind not size as in AGENTS.md:88).
principle_conflict: P2: the iteration-folder workflow itself is repo-specific methodology
atoms.proof_purpose: the contract's coverage matrix has no zero row (criterion without a check) and no zero column (check that covers no criterion)
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE at contract acceptance: extend G1's coverage-matrix check (acceptance criteria x deterministic checks) to reject zero columns as well as zero rows, and write the contract and its first ledger entry in one journaled step so no task exists without its contract.

atoms.name: nba: one next action with done-when
atoms.statement: nba reads live cycle state and returns exactly one next action, the cheapest move that clears the binding constraint, framed as where you are, the action, why now and an observable done-when, without executing it.
atoms.mechanism: skills/coil/nba/SKILL.md:10 (one action, no menu), 14-18 (workflow), 22-28 (one action; state-grounded; the avoided move over busywork; external input when no outside truth enters; read-only; no auto-invoking user-only skills), 34-37 (cites state, exactly one action, done-when).
principle_conflict: Z3: in paperthin a model picks the action; G1 must derive it deterministically
atoms.proof_purpose: none (guidance; the Stop gate, not the reason text, is the enforcement)
atoms.g1_design: INJECT through the Stop continue reason: G1 names exactly one failing acceptance check from its pass/fail vector (deterministic tie-break such as contract order) and gives that check's exact command as the done-when, instead of a list or a model-written plan.

atoms.name: catchup: state-grounded re-entry briefing
atoms.statement: catchup rebuilds a returning human's context from live state rather than conversation memory, anchored at their last touch and ordered as needs-you, changed and new words, with every claim traceable to a file, commit or artifact and 'done' meaning verified done.
atoms.mechanism: skills/coil/catchup/SKILL.md:18-21 (read live state; anchor; delta), 22-28 (decision order), 36 (every claim traces to a source), 42 (honest completeness), 49-52 (verification).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection
principle_conflict: Z4: in paperthin the briefing is model-written; G1's projection must be generated by G1 from its ledger
atoms.proof_purpose: none (projection supporting TW(b) reconstruction)
atoms.g1_design: INJECT: G1's SessionStart projection lists the active task, its contract hash, the latest receipt and the delta since that receipt, each line citing ledger sequence and hash, and shows 'complete' only for receipt-bound completions.

atoms.name: mandela: verifier must not be the designer
atoms.statement: mandela audits any validation against eight leakage patterns, including shared hallucination, tautology (a scorer grading buckets it drew) and verifier = designer, and asks whether external ground truth enters independently.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/mandela/SKILL.md:14-17 (identify components; the core question), 21-28 (the eight patterns), 32 (a blinded output can still leak through the collection recipe), 34 (optional blind N=1 auditor), 40-42 (apply patterns 3-5 to the audit itself).
atoms.proof_purpose: the checks that produced the receipt are byte-identical to the checks fixed in the contract before work began, so the agent did not author or weaken its own verifier during the task
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE: at contract time G1 hashes every file its checks depend on (tests, fixtures, verifier scripts) as declared in the contract; PreToolUse denies writes to them during the task, and the completion gate at Stop requires their hashes to equal the contract-time hashes, else deny. This makes patterns 4 and 5 mechanical; T1's tree binding alone would bind tests the agent had already weakened.

atoms.name: sip: post-change self-check orchestrator
atoms.statement: sip is a model-invoked skill that, right after any create or change, runs shower, factchk or mandela, an ssotize audit, detool and re0 on the result, on the stated premise that 'remember to verify' never fires in a fresh session.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/sip/SKILL.md:10 (premise), 14-20 (workflow), 24-28 (rules), 34-36 (verification); README.md:302-315. It is still description-triggered with no hook (docs/invocation.md:6), so its 'automatic' firing is fail-open.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks (Stop audit with a fast judge model)
principle_conflict: Z1: 'automatic' depends on the model choosing to invoke it
P4: its checks are model judgments, not deterministic verification
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT the skill. Its own premise, that prompt reminders do not fire, is the case for G1's Stop hook running G1's deterministic verification whenever the agent tries to stop.

atoms.name: shower: zero-context cold read
atoms.statement: shower hands a fresh, context-free sub-session only the artifact's contents, never a repo path or the author's intent, compares its blind reading with a privately noted intent, treats every mismatch as a defect, and warns that one read is one draw.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/shower/SKILL.md:14-21 (workflow), 25-30 (separate sub-session; no intent; forced assumptions are findings; a single draw; read, don't sweep), 36-37 (verification); the only evidence is one anecdote (README.md:233-242).
principle_conflict: P4: a model's reading is a measurement, never a gate
atoms.proof_purpose: measurement fact: a fresh agy session given only G1's projection reconstructs the active task and next failing check at rate p (with CI)
atoms.g1_design: MEASURE TW(b): run N fresh agy sessions that receive only G1's SessionStart projection, score whether each names the right task, contract hash and next failing check, and report the rate with a confidence interval; a regression blocks a G1 release, never agent work.

atoms.name: detool: no incidental host nouns in portable text
atoms.statement: detool classifies text by role and replaces incidental vendor, model, CLI, path or harness nouns in durable content with the mechanism they mean, while keeping provenance, runbooks and tool-subject claims concrete; durable docs also use generic examples rather than real instances and never model-brand a name.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/detool/SKILL.md:10-12 (goal), 16-23 (role before edit; mechanism, not euphemism), 27-33 (rules); AGENTS.md:8 (generic examples, not instances); AGENTS.md:37 (never model-brand a name); skills/depth/modelchk/SKILL.md:52 (no concrete model names in durable mechanism text).
atoms.proof_purpose: G1 core files contain no host identifiers outside the agy adapter
atoms.g1_design: ENFORCE in G1's test suite: a deterministic grep over G1 core, excluding the adapter directory, for a host-noun list (agy, antigravity, gemini, agy event and file names) must return zero hits; role judgments stay with human reviewers.

atoms.name: re0: rewrite a drifted artifact as v0
atoms.statement: re0 rewrites a drifted artifact as if it were the first clean version, converting 'what changed' into 'what is true now' and repairing from the source of truth rather than the damaged surface.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/re0/SKILL.md:10 (goal), 14-23 (workflow), 27-34 (rules, including 29 'what is true now' and 33 repair from the source of truth), 38 (cold re-read); README.md:129-142.
principle_conflict: PH and P2: rewriting artifacts is the agent's native work
P3: a rewrite erases history that G1's ledger must keep
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as a G1 mechanism. Its useful split, append-only history plus a regenerated 'what is true now' view, is already G1's ledger and projection.

atoms.name: readchk: restate before spending work
atoms.statement: readchk restates a long or ambiguous instruction internally in different words, cross-checks it against context, proceeds silently when context resolves it, asks one specific question when a real fork survives, and logs an 'understood as' line for substantial work.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/readchk/SKILL.md:16-21 (workflow, with the durable 'understood as' line at 21), 25-29 (rules), 33 (verification); README.md:144-155.
principle_conflict: PH: improves understanding rather than preventing loss or false completion
Z3 and Z4: the 'understood as' line is agent-authored and unverifiable
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT. G1 anchors intent in the immutable contract's deterministic acceptance checks, which do not depend on how the agent paraphrased the request.

atoms.name: aim: propose intent instead of asking
atoms.statement: aim reads handed-over data end to end and proposes the likely intent for the user to confirm, rather than asking an open question.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/aim/SKILL.md:10 (goal), 14-17 (workflow), 21-25 (rules), 29 (verification: the user's reply is short).
principle_conflict: PH: interaction quality, not durability or verification
P8: proves no fact
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT.

atoms.name: modelchk: size tier and effort, no routing
atoms.statement: modelchk recommends the cheapest sufficient capability tier and a reasoning-effort intent on neutral scales, with move-up and move-down triggers and a separate proof surface, and claims no routing authority.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/modelchk/SKILL.md:8 (advisory, no routing), 12-27 (two dials), 31-42 (workflow), 46-56 (rules, including 51 no routing authority and 54 'a stronger tier or a higher effort never replaces tests'), 60-67 (output schema).
principle_conflict: G1 scope: the model is fixed and effort is always high, so there is nothing to size
P8: advice with no proof purpose
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT. Its one transferable rule, that more capability or effort never replaces verification, is already P4.

atoms.name: hate: one root objection, cheapest falsifier
atoms.statement: hate attacks a plan along named failure axes, collapses the findings into one load-bearing root objection, and returns the cheapest falsifying experiment (the 'first nail') instead of a checklist.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/hate/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 15-19 (workflow and attack axes), 23-24 (rules), 30-31 (verification); it is user-invoked to avoid a demolition bias (docs/invocation.md:16); README.md:170-183.
principle_conflict: PH: sharpens reasoning rather than preventing loss
G1 control math: Hamming distance and displacement need the full pass/fail vector, so fail-fast truncation of checks would destroy information
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT. G1's authority gate already fails on any failing check, and its control layer must evaluate every check instead of stopping at the first.

atoms.name: feynman: press a decision via isolated critic
atoms.statement: feynman has an isolated critic press a just-made decision one gap at a time, narrowing instead of repeating and never supplying the rationale first, ending when every gap is explained or one is named and flagged.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/feynman/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 15-22 (workflow), 26-30 (rules), 34-37 (verification).
principle_conflict: PH: a human-understanding aid
P6: requires a human in the loop
P8: proves no fact
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT.

atoms.name: autobahn: carve risky scope, clean-room run
atoms.statement: autobahn carves guardrail-adjacent items out of scope with safe alternatives, runs the remainder in a fresh subagent that sees only the carved prompt and is barred from logs, notes and transcript search, and writes the descope ledger and archive only after the run closes.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/autobahn/SKILL.md:14-19 (FRAME, CARVE, GUARD, RUN, VERIFY, LEDGER), 23 and 38 (bar on shared logs, notes and transcripts), 19, 31 and 41 (archive written after the run); README.md:198-211 reports zero flags and zero refusals.
principle_conflict: Z1-Z3: deliberately withholds the original request and the session's reasoning from the executing agent and bars it from shared records
P3: defers durable records until after the run, so a crash mid-run loses the descope ledger
P8: proves no G1 fact
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT. G1 never hides inputs or records from audit, and its write-ahead journal is the opposite of autobahn's write-after archive. An explicit exclusions list is already served by the contract's declared scope (PTH-29).

atoms.name: reorder: move items only, one principle
atoms.statement: reorder realigns a drifted listing under one nameable principle, moving items only (nothing reworded, added or removed) and keeping mirrored copies in identical order.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/reorder/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 15-19 (workflow), 23-27 (rules), 31-34 (verification); README.md:259-270.
principle_conflict: P8: cosmetic; its permutation invariant is already covered by the declared-scope invariant (PTH-29)
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT.

atoms.name: dedash: remove em-dashes by grammatical role
atoms.statement: dedash removes em-dashes and look-alikes from a user-owned scope one occurrence at a time, choosing replacement punctuation by grammatical role and leaving hyphens, ranges and code alone.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/dedash/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 15-27 (FIND, REPLACE, LEAVE-ALONE, RE-READ, REPORT), 31-34 (rules).
principle_conflict: P8: stylistic; proves no fact
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT.

atoms.name: debloat: compress to load-bearing density
atoms.statement: debloat compresses correct but verbose prose to its load-bearing density, cutting words but never a rule, fact, constraint or example, and hands duplication to ssotize and drift to re0.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/debloat/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 15-20 (workflow), 24-29 (rules), 35-37 (verification).
principle_conflict: P8: authoring aid; the length of G1's injected text is better settled by A/B measurement than by a compression habit
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT.

atoms.name: factchk: verify claims in both directions
atoms.statement: factchk verifies reality-grounded claims against external sources in both directions (the absurd may be real, the obvious may be false), fixes clear errors with a citation, flags judgment calls, and flags rather than asserts when no source is reachable.
atoms.mechanism: skills/depth/factchk/SKILL.md:10 (goal), 14-17 (workflow, including web search at 15), 21-24 (rules), 28 (verification); README.md:272-285.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct (confirm against a primary source, or stop and surface)
principle_conflict: P4: web lookups are non-deterministic and cannot sit in the authority path
PH: improves the agent's claims rather than preventing false completion
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT; its 'flag, never assert, when unreachable' rule is covered by G1's UNKNOWN state (PTH-30).

atoms.name: ssotize: audit, approve, consolidate to one home
atoms.statement: ssotize names one fact, audits every occurrence read-only, picks the canonical home, reports a mutation plan, and only after explicit approval folds unique details in and replaces copies with references, never silently resolving contradictions or consolidating across a trust boundary.
atoms.mechanism: skills/breadth/ssotize/SKILL.md:10-14 (goal; read-only first), 18-29 (workflow), 33-41 (rules: 34 read-only audit, 36 contradictions kept separate, 38 trust boundary), 47-52 (verification); README.md:244-257.
principle_conflict: P6: requires per-plan human approval
PH: repository hygiene is the agent's native work
atoms.proof_purpose: none beyond the ledger's
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as a mechanism; its rules already hold in G1: the ledger is the single home, a disagreement between ledger and tree marks a completion stale instead of being silently reconciled, and agent-channel data never merges into the trusted ledger.

atoms.name: re0-loop: build-QA-memo-restart cycle
atoms.statement: re0-loop runs FRAME, BUILD, DRIVE, RE0-MEMO, HATE, RE0-WORK cycles, measures progress by quality-cleared templates and eliminated anti-patterns, treats tests as supporting evidence rather than the gate, and stops a lap when no outside truth enters.
atoms.mechanism: skills/coil/re0-loop/SKILL.md:13 (cycle), 16 (unit of progress), 20-26 (workflow), 30-35 (rules: 30 tests are not the gate, 35 stop a lap without outside truth), 41-44 (verification); README.md:332-343.
principle_conflict: P4: 'tests are supporting evidence, not the gate' inverts G1, where deterministic checks are the gate
P2: build methodology is the agent's native work
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT the loop. Its stop rule (no new outside truth, no new lap) is already G1's Stop control: a continuation requires displacement in the pass/fail vector since the previous one.

atoms.name: re0-work: restart from v0, keep earned contracts
atoms.statement: re0-work restarts from v0, keeping only the contracts, schemas, gates, vocabulary, real-surface tests and negative corpus that earned reuse, and names the first gate before planning one vertical loop.
atoms.mechanism: skills/coil/re0-work/SKILL.md:10 (goal), 14-19 (workflow), 23-28 (rules), 34-37 (verification).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with a contract hash
principle_conflict: P2: restart decisions belong to the native agent
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT; 'start fresh but keep earned contracts and gates' is what G1 already gives a fresh agent through the ledger and immutable contracts.
encodes: keep the contract, drop the implementation

atoms.name: prism: independent lenses, never average
atoms.statement: prism splits one artifact across 2-5 independent lenses, one per distinct failure mode, each giving a one-line verdict, and returns where they agree plus the single question that would resolve any disagreement, never an average.
atoms.mechanism: skills/mesh/prism/SKILL.md:11 (goal), 15-20 (workflow), 24-30 (rules), 34 (verification).
principle_conflict: P4: lens verdicts are model judgments
P8 and PH: proves no fact and aims to make the AI smarter
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT; its never-average rule already matches G1's no-statistics-in-authority placement (PTH-34).

atoms.name: Recursive dogfooding presented as proof
atoms.statement: Every skill is meant to be usable while building the skills, so the suite maintains itself with its own skills and presents those self-applications as its proof.
atoms.mechanism: AGENTS.md:11 states the recursion; the README [PROOF] blocks mostly apply a skill to its own repository or spec (README.md:136-142, 233-242, 279-285, 309-315, 322-330).
principle_conflict: Z2 and Z5: a designer verifying with its own tools is mandela's pattern 5, verifier = designer
P4: anecdotes are not deterministic verification
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: REJECT as evidence. G1 may be used on its own development, but its trust comes from negative controls and independent deterministic checks, not from self-application stories.

adoption_candidates: PTH-41: freeze the files the contract's checks depend on, deny writes to them, and require hash equality at completion; this closes the gap where tree binding would bind tests the agent had already weakened.
PTH-29: a declared write scope, enforced by a PreToolUse deny plus an exact changed-path subset check at Stop, turns 'only these paths change' into a proof.
PTH-14: a negative-control fixture for every gate proves the gate can fail, the most direct way to meet P8's 'name the fact it proves'.

PTH-11: exact equality for every duplicated fact, applied to G1's hooks.json registrations and script hashes and checked by the global root-of-trust PreToolUse, catches an agent that rewrote hooks.json for the next session.
PTH-12: strict canonical parsing (duplicate keys rejected before hashing) gives every ledger, contract and receipt record exactly one meaning; cheap, and tested upstream.
PTH-19: an idempotent, non-clobbering bootstrap that classifies hook entries as current, stale or foreign and verifies the post-state by set equality.
PTH-31: two independent enumerations of the changed set (git and a content-hash walk) must agree, which makes the scope and tree checks complete.
PTH-30: tri-state results where UNKNOWN denies like FAIL; keep T1's behavior and make it explicit.
PTH-33: gate decisions as pure functions of ledger state and tool arguments, with exact-repeat denials counted as revisits.
PTH-21: a measured, version-keyed agy hook contract; paperthin's stale 'Antigravity has no session-start event' claim shows why documented capabilities are not enough.
PTH-38: reject zero columns as well as zero rows in the contract coverage matrix.
PTH-10: one constants module for state paths, a tombstone grep for deleted mechanisms, and fail-closed on unknown ledger schema versions.
PTH-16: deny agent writes to G1 state, receipts, hooks.json files and verifier entry points.
PTH-15: an idempotent completion append keyed by (task, receipt hash), with the exact identity check immediately before it.
PTH-39: the Stop continue reason names exactly one failing check, with its command as the done-when.
PTH-40: SessionStart projection lines cite ledger sequence and hash and show the delta since the last receipt.
PTH-36: default-deny admission of new G1 mechanisms unless they mechanize an existing proof obligation.
PTH-35: every observed G1 failure class becomes a deterministic regression fixture.
PTH-44: a host-noun grep over G1 core enforces P7.
PTH-43: measure TW(b) with fresh agy sessions that see only the projection.
PTH-07: A/B-test the wording of injected text on the false-completion rate in the measurement layer.
risks: Supply chain: re0-upgrade downloads executable hook scripts from raw.githubusercontent.com by tag into ~/.re0/ and registers them as SessionStart commands in ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.codex/config.toml with no checksum (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:65-67), while the release policy allows deleting and re-cutting a tag at the same version (AGENTS.md:109; skills/depth/re0-release/SKILL.md:29), so the 'pinned' code can change.

Prompt supply chain: installation uses unpinned npx skills@latest, recommends an elevated/admin shell, and creates auto-updating symlinks, so upstream SKILL.md edits flow straight into every agent's standing instructions (README.md:23-26); README.md:29 invites users to paste the command into an agent and say 'set this up for me'.

Network call with user credentials: after an upgrade the skill offers to star the repository through the user's authenticated gh account with gh api -X PUT user/starred/LilMGenius/paperthin (skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:70-74); it is consent-gated but is a promotional side effect inside an install flow.

Safety-pattern concern: autobahn is model-invoked with a broad trigger ('fires on the impulse ... brace for a refusal') and runs work in a subagent that never sees the original risky request and is barred from logs and transcripts (skills/depth/autobahn/SKILL.md:3,10,16-17,23); README.md:209 reports 'zero flags, zero refusals'. Despite the non-evasion disclaimer (skills/depth/autobahn/SKILL.md:29), the design isolates the executor from safety-relevant context.

Injected instruction text: the SessionStart hook injects model-directed instructions ('tell the user they can run /re0-upgrade ... do NOT run /re0-upgrade') (scripts/catalog.cjs:66-70); every model-invoked SKILL.md is instruction text that fires on a description match (docs/invocation.md:6), and factchk directs web lookups (skills/depth/factchk/SKILL.md:15).

Evidence quality: README [PROOF] blocks (for example README.md:136-142 and README.md:205-211) and code rationales (scripts/catalog.cjs:12,63-65,37) point into the gitignored .re0/ directory (.gitignore:3; AGENTS.md:75), so they cannot be verified; scripts/check-frontmatter.test.cjs:8-15 is the only test in the repository, and no other guard has a negative test.
Unverified external claims: README.md:203 cites a suspension of named frontier models and a GPT-5.6 release as prior art; these were not verified here and should be treated as repository claims only.
Destructive helper: scripts/link-skills.sh:32-33 runs rm -rf on any existing non-symlink directory in ~/.claude/skills whose name matches a skill.

Stale host claim: skills/breadth/re0-upgrade/SKILL.md:68 says Antigravity CLI has no session-start event, which contradicts G1's measured agy 1.1.27 SessionStart support, while README.md:9 lists Antigravity as supported.

Fail-open delivery: CLAUDE.md:1 holds only the bare text 'AGENTS.md' (a regular file, not an @-import or a symlink), so AGENTS.md:81's claim that Claude Code 'reaches it through the one-line CLAUDE.md' depends on the model choosing to open the file.

Guard coverage gaps: scripts/check-catalog-sync.cjs:6 says '21-skill roster' for a 28-name catalog (scripts/catalog.cjs:19-24), the sync guard checks set equality but not order (AGENTS.md:86), and agreement of the invocation flags across frontmatter, README and docs/invocation.md is not guarded (it is currently consistent).

Clock-based throttle: the 24-hour notice throttle has no lower bound, so a ~/.re0/last-notice.json dated in the future suppresses notices until 24 hours after that date, and one stamp is shared by all hosts (scripts/session-check.cjs:34-38; scripts/catalog.cjs:38-39).

Telemetry: none found. The runtime scripts only read ~/.agents/skills and ~/.claude/skills and write ~/.re0/last-notice.json (scripts/catalog.cjs:29-32,38-39; scripts/session-check.cjs:41-46); network use is confined to re0-upgrade (npx, raw.githubusercontent.com, gh api), factchk web lookups, and release CI (.github/workflows/release.yml:33-57).

License: MIT (LICENSE:1-3). NOTICE:1-2 says some material is vendored verbatim from mattpocock/skills (MIT) but tracks attribution per source rather than per file, so the vendored files cannot be identified.

coverage: All 65 files were read (static analysis only; nothing from the repository was installed or executed). The English README, AGENTS.md, docs/invocation.md, all 28 SKILL.md files, all scripts, workflows and configs, and the three SVG assets were read in full; the SVGs are text-only, with no scripts or external references. The ten localized READMEs were compared structurally and found identical (same 138-line layout, same skill-link order, the same four URLs, the same install command, the same set of code tokens, no HTML comments or hidden characters); the Korean copy was read in full and the Spanish and German copies in part. There are no binaries, weights or data files. The clone is shallow (one commit, one tag, v0.17.7).
